name: Hairmogging

card.summary: Looking better than someone else on the strength of hair (fullness, hairline, style), the looksmaxxing term for the visual advantage of a full head of hair over a balding man.

quick.overview:
Hairmogging is looksmaxxing slang for out-looking another person because of one's hair, for example a man with a full hairline standing next to a balding one. 'Mogging' means visually outclassing someone. It frames hair as an appearance lever people can protect or improve.

Research cited by Wikipedia says pattern hair loss affects about half of men by 50 and that thinning is associated with worries about looking older or less attractive, though meta-analyses found distress moderate on average.
quick.how: Followers pursue it by keeping hair (finasteride, minoxidil), restoring it (transplants) or choosing styles to suit skull and hairline; a forum answer says hair length can be used to frame or hide the face.
quick.risks: The practice itself has no direct risks; the treatments involved carry their own, such as sexual side effects of finasteride or surgical risks of transplants.

lead: Hairmogging is a looksmaxxing term for gaining an advantage in appearance through hair, typically a full head of hair compared with a balding man. 'Mogging' is community slang for visually outclassing another person.

About half of men develop pattern hair loss by age 50, and Wikipedia reports that hair is associated with youth and vigor in men, with thinning linked to worry about appearing older or less attractive.[1] Two meta-analyses found psychosocial distress moderate on average.[1]
In forum discussion, users compare how hairstyle and hairline interact with skull shape, with one reply saying skull shape matters most and advising hair length that frames the face.[2]

angle.text: Followers aim to keep or style hair so it works in their favour relative to peers.

paras: The term describes a hair-based mog, where hair is the deciding factor in a comparison. Treatments mentioned in general sources for hair preservation include finasteride, topical minoxidil and hair transplants; shaving is also a standard option.[1]
On looksmax.org users debate whether short hair outperforms longer hair given a good hairline, with responses citing skull shape and hairline.[2]
No studies found on hairmogging as such. Studies of hair loss and its psychosocial effects are summarised in general references.[1]

lore.intro: Hairmogging comes up in threads comparing hairstyles and hairlines.[2]

claims.claim: Skull shape determines which hairstyles work.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org reply says it is all about skull shape and that people with less defined faces can grow hair to frame the face.[2]
claims.experts: No published study has tested this claim.
